newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan police stop march for killer of Israelis.
newsitem.headline: Jordan police stop march for killer of Israelis.

text.p: Police in northern Jordan used teargas on Tuesday to break up a march in support of a soldier jailed for life for killing seven Israeli schoolgirls, witnesses said.

They said police blocked demonstrators including the wife and mother of army private Ahmed Daqamsa, sentenced in a military court on Saturday, who were heading from Daqamsa's village of Ibdr to the nearby town of Irbid.
They said around 150 to 200 marchers, waving placards calling for Daqamsa's release and protesting his trial was unfair, set out from Ibdr, about 80 km (50 miles) north of Amman.
Police brought in reinforcements by helicopter, blocked the road to Irbid and used teargas to disperse the marchers, the witnesses said.
"Police came and blocked the marchers and hit them," Ahmed Mustafa Daqamsa, the soldier's uncle, told Reuters by telephone.
"Some of the youths protested the beatings of the women and they were arrested," he said. He said roads in and out of Ibdr were still blocked by police.
Another witness who asked not to be identified said only one person was arrested.
Daqamsa was sentenced on Saturday to life imprisonment for killing the seven Israeli girls on the border territory of Baqoura in March.
The panel of military judges ruled the killings were deliberate but said Daqamsa suffered from a mental problem which meant he could not have planned the killings beforehand.
On Sunday over 1,000 students at Jordan university marched in support of Daqamsa, chanting anti-Israeli slogans and burning a cardboard replica of the Israeli flag.
Jordan and Israel signed a peace treaty in 1994.
